drivingQuestion: Does 'both are liable' show that damage by innocuous oxen may be collected from either ox?
outcomeNote: Rav Ashi's reply continues in the next unit (sugya132)

segments.he: הָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם שֶׁל אִישׁ אֶחָד – שְׁנֵיהֶם חַיָּיבִים. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִפַּרְזִיקָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, שְׁוָורִים תַּמִּים שֶׁהִזִּיקוּ – רָצָה מִזֶּה גּוֹבֶה, רָצָה מִזֶּה גּוֹבֶה.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: In a case where an ox was injured by one of two oxen that were pursuing it, if «both» oxen «belonged to one person, both are liable. Rava of Parzika said to Rav Ashi:» Should one «learn from» the fact that both are liable that in a case of «innocuous oxen that caused damage,» if the injured party «wishes,» he can «collect» damages «from» the proceeds from the sale of «this» ox, and if «he wishes,» he can «collect from» the sale of «that» ox?
